title: Employer Gifts Up to ₹15,000 Now Tax-Free: What Salaried Taxpayers Need to Know
description: The annual tax-free limit for employer-provided gifts, vouchers, or tokens has been increased. The new limit for such gifts is now ₹15,000, up from the previo.

faq.q: What is the new tax-free limit for employer gifts?
faq.a: The new tax-free limit for employer-provided gifts, vouchers, or tokens is ₹15,000 in an aggregate financial year. This is a significant increase from the previous limit of ₹5,000.

faq.q: Does this limit apply to cash gifts from my employer?
faq.a: No, this exemption primarily applies to non-monetary gifts, gift vouchers, or tokens that are not directly convertible into cash. Cash payments, even if termed as gifts, are generally treated as salary or bonus and are fully taxable.

faq.q: What if I receive gifts from multiple employers in the same financial year?
faq.a: The ₹15,000 limit applies per employer. If you work for multiple employers in a financial year and receive gifts from each, the ₹15,000 limit would apply separately to the gifts received from each employer.

faq.q: Is this a per-occasion limit or an annual limit?
faq.a: This is an aggregate annual limit. The total value of all eligible gifts received from a single employer during the financial year (April 1st to March 31st) must not exceed ₹15,000 to be fully tax-free.

faq.q: How will my employer account for gifts exceeding the limit?
faq.a: If the total value of gifts exceeds ₹15,000, the excess amount will be added to your taxable income as a 'perquisite'. Your employer will typically include this taxable perquisite in your salary slip and Form 16, deducting TDS if applicable.

faq.q: Are gift cards or vouchers considered non-monetary?
faq.a: Yes, generally, gift cards or vouchers that are redeemable for goods or services and not directly convertible into cash are considered non-monetary for the purpose of this exemption.
